material_flags.span: When Murad II unified the Ottoman realm
material_flags.reason: Mohammed/Mahomet reunited it. His son Murad later reversed Manuel's gains. The same model answered H4-Q1 correctly.

material_flags.span: Finally, John VIII.
material_flags.reason: The supplied text calls this ruler JohnVI throughout. The output switches toVIII after itself usingVI; source matching must not silently correct Oman.

material_flags.span: physical decay of Constantinople and its economic dependence on Italian merchants
material_flags.reason: Cites365, which introduces descriptions; specific physical decay and Italian commercial control appear on366.

material_flags.span: these gains were reversed when Murad II unified the Turkish realm
material_flags.reason: Mohammed reunified the realm; Murad's later war reversed the gains. Also cites360 before either development.
material_flags.origin: recurrent in independent full-source control, not propagated

material_flags.span: This religious shift coexisted with a literary revival under the Macedonian dynasty
material_flags.reason: Links fourth/sixth-century Christianization and ascetic withdrawal to ninth/tenth-century literary rulers as coexisting, inventing a relation across the gaps.

material_flags.span: The last emperor, John VIII
material_flags.reason: The source says the last John Paleologus, not the last emperor. It calls himJohnVI. The sentence also cites366 rather than367 for Florence and Western aid.
material_flags.origin: new last-emperor claim in independent control; imperial-number issue recurs independently

material_flags.span: ended gladiatorial games in Constantinople
material_flags.reason: The source says Christian Constantinople never knew gladiatorial games; the surviving games were at Rome.

material_flags.span: Theodosius I’s moral crusade, including the spectacular death of the monk Telemachus
material_flags.reason: The source explicitly distinguishes Theodosius’s state measures from Telemachus’s later individual action, saying abolition was not the work of the State.

material_flags.span: Leo VI the Wise and his grandson Constantine VII
material_flags.reason: Leo is Basil’s son and Constantine his grandson. Constantine is Leo’s son, not Leo’s grandson.

material_flags.span: was retaken when the attack was delayed a few weeks
material_flags.reason: The source says the town could have been rescued if its fall had been delayed. It was captured; the raiders departed with booty. No successful delayed rescue is narrated.

material_flags.span: repelled only by a “miraculous vision of the Virgin”
material_flags.judgment: causal contradiction and lost report status
material_flags.reason: Walls repelled the assault; the report of a vision encouraged resistance. Mustapha’s rebellion caused Murad to lift the siege. The output makes the vision the sole cause and removes report status.

material_flags.span: only isolated enclaves—African cities and the Italian Exarchate—still preserved the language
material_flags.reason: Source also preserves Dalmatian ports and scattered Balkan survivors. Africa/Italy are the only districts with a considerable Latin population still obeying the emperor, not all surviving Latin speakers.

nonmaterial_review_notes: Gemma's Bulgarian invasion wording can mean an invasion involving Bulgaria; source says an invasion of Bulgaria. Mark ambiguous wording, not a proved reversal.
Gemma's broad new-development-in-warfare phrase may overgeneralize the source's first German race to adopt cavalry, but remains attributed and ambiguous; do not force a contradiction.
Qwen's Roman flanks plural broadens the specifically left-flank cavalry charge. Treat as minor precision loss.

Adjacent-page locator drift occurs for Valens's character, Lupicinus's food policy, literary achievements, methodical compiler, Manuel's recovered territories, and urban exhaustion. Preserve these separately from material factual claims.
Gemma full-source control uses three H1 paragraphs plus one H3 paragraph. It omits all H2 and H4 coverage despite having four paragraphs.
Qwen full-source control uses two H1 paragraphs, combines H2/H3 in one paragraph, and uses one H4 paragraph. Four paragraphs alone does not satisfy one paragraph per passage.
Both full-source controls use parenthesized page numbers, not the instructed physical-PDF citation syntax.
Qwen merged output appears to reproduce the four direct summaries verbatim in order; verify exact normalized equality programmatically.
No whole-source claims from controls are classified inherited: they did not receive direct summaries. Same-family recurrence is independent.

GPT H4 summary says gains vanished after Mohammed’s1421 reunification. Because the loss occurred later, after is not itself a demonstrated false date or claim that Mohammed caused it. Record omitted Murad/claimant causation in coverage.

GPT assigns the bailiff observation to John’s recognition, whereas the source attributes the remark to Manuel. Record attribution precision separately; do not automatically turn this into a fabricated event.
GPT H3 describes a failed Bulgarian invasion, which remains ambiguous between an invasion by or of Bulgaria. No hard reversal is counted.
GPT full-source control mislabels H1 as61–66 and H2 as169–170, while supplied ranges were61–67 and169–176. It omits H2’s entire religious/social section.
GPT full-source control calls John’s reign brief without source support for that characterization. Record this as an unsupported evaluative qualifier.

The source gives two rebellions total, with the second after blinding. Listing twice, then blinding, then again can suggest three. It can also be a retrospective total followed by details; no hard contradiction counted.
